clue.text: The sucker! — doing domestic work!

parts.note: a sucker sounds like a dupe, but here it is a household appliance that sucks up dust while the chores get done

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' tempts you towards a gullible person; it is literal, a machine that sucks dirt from carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: The household appliance draws dust in by suction, so it is quite literally a sucker used for housework.

clue.text: The crowning glory

parts.note: the phrase usually means a supreme achievement, but read literally it is a glorious radiance worn like a crown around a holy figure's head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowning glory' is an idiom for a finest achievement; literally it is the halo of light round a saint's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo or circle of light painted around the head of a saint is a radiance that crowns them.

clue.text: Raised as an arrow-poison tree

parts.note: something raised is up
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that some tree was cultivated to provide poison for arrows.
explanation.walkthrough: The UPAS is a Javanese tree whose sap was used to tip poisoned arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asian upas tree yields a toxic latex traditionally smeared on hunting darts and arrowheads.

clue.text: Teams playing say for a Welsh town

indicators.note: teams that are playing are in action, which signals the word teams being rearranged

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: Sports teams are performing in a fixture at a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges TEAMS into MAEST, and EG follows. Maesteg is a town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Maesteg is a former mining town in Bridgend county, South Wales.

clue.text: Orderly has to remain outside, it's ruled

indicators.note: the word for remain stays outside, wrapping around the word for orderly

parts.note: to remain in place is to lie, as in 'lie fallow'
orderly means neat and tidy

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly must wait outside while a ruling is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital attendant but is an adjective here; 'outside' puts LIE around NEAT. 'has to' and 'it's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineate describes something marked with lines, as ruled paper is.

clue.text: A redhead child can be so mischievous!

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired kid has a reputation for being naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' is read as the head of 'red', giving R; 'can be so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch look or smile is playfully knowing and teasing, a synonym for roguish.

clue.text: Passed in a decent obscurity

indicators.note: letters in obscurity are muddled and unclear, which signals that a decent is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone respectable died quietly, unremarked and in obscurity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed' suggests dying; it means made law. 'obscurity' rearranges A DECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that has been passed by parliament has been made law.

clue.text: Following a style — to a certain extent

parts.note: following means coming after
taken as written
a style is a fashion

explanation.surface: Copying a fashion, though only partially.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, but it splits cleanly into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something in a rough or partial way, only somewhat.

clue.text: Romantically directed, single males agree

parts.note: something directed somewhere is sent there
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit
males are men
to tally is to agree or match

explanation.surface: A matchmaking scheme in which unattached men consent to romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single males' looks like one phrase about bachelors; it splits into I and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a soppy, emotional, tender way is acting with feeling about love.

clue.text: Kneading of bread may be prohibited

indicators.note: kneading works dough over and over, signalling the letters of of bread being reworked

explanation.surface: A warning that bread-making may be banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kneading' rearranges OF BREAD; 'may be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbade is the past tense of forbid, to ban or disallow.

clue.text: Blink on seeing shoddy stuff in fine surroundings

indicators.note: the word for fine forms the surroundings, enclosing the word for shoddy stuff

parts.note: fine means nice
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: Someone flinches on spotting cheap junk in an elegant setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fine surroundings' puts TAT inside NICE. TAT is British slang for cheap, tacky goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictate is the technical term for winking or quickly shutting the eyelids.

clue.text: Bearing present that's no longer enough

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
the present is now

explanation.surface: A gift that once satisfied no longer suffices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing present' reads as carrying a gift; it is a compass point E plus NOW. 'no longer' marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Enow is an old poetic form meaning sufficient, now obsolete in everyday speech.

clue.text: To cook meat's tricky

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward to handle, so the letters of meat's are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive spelling supplies its S as a letter here

explanation.surface: Preparing meat is a difficult business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges the five letters of MEAT'S, the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is a method of preparing food over boiling water.

clue.text: Reinstatement order

parts.note: an instruction to a printer or typesetter to restore something that was struck out, read like a legal order of reinstatement

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a court ruling restoring someone to a job; it is the proofreader's Latin mark 'let it stand'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proofreading mark tells the typesetter to ignore a deletion and keep the original text.

clue.text: Just a little bit off course

definitions.text: Just a little bit off course

parts.words: Just a little bit off course
parts.note: it sounds like a slight navigational error, but it is a small piece of turf literally taken off a golf course by a club

explanation.walkthrough: 'off course' suggests straying; read literally it is a scrap of turf hacked off the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's swing gouges a small clod of grass out of the fairway.

clue.text: Native Americans go around quietly, and that's material

indicators.note: the people named go around, enclosing the letter for quietly

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Native Americans move silently, and the scene is described as fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go around' puts P inside CREE; 'and that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin fabric with a crinkled surface.

clue.text: Getting less money in a wallet

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for money sits inside the word for wallet

parts.note: a wallet is a kind of bag
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone finding the cash in their purse dwindling.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for money; 'in' puts it inside BAG, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is abating is diminishing or subsiding.

clue.text: The noble dignity of the properly-treated old mare

indicators.note: letters properly treated are reworked into correct order, signalling old mare being rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocratic sense of dignity shown in caring well for an aged horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properly-treated' rearranges OLD MARE; 'of the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank or title of an earl, a peerage.

clue.text: Men at sea having caught over five hundred slip away

parts.note: ABs, able seamen, are sailors
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
over can mean on, as in a dispute on or over something
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Sailors, having captured more than five hundred prisoners, escape.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is an able-bodied seaman; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to flee secretly, especially to escape the law.

clue.text: Dispatch including suggestion for an allowance

indicators.note: the word for dispatch includes, or holds inside, the word for suggestion

parts.note: to dispatch is to send
a tip is a hint or suggestion

explanation.surface: A message proposing a payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' looks like a noun meaning message; it is the verb SEND. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment, such as a clergyman's salary or a student grant.

clue.text: The most expert get fed-up with experiment

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word fed is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an experiment is a test

explanation.surface: Even the best specialists grow tired of endless trials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed-up' reads as bored; it splits into FED and 'up', which turns it to DEF in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Deftest is the superlative of deft, meaning skilful or nimble.

clue.text: Turner excels. Brown is behind

indicators.note: the word for brown comes behind, after the word for excels

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo it
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: An art critic rating the painter Turner above a lesser artist named Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests J.M.W. Turner, the English painter; it is anything that turns. A capstan is a revolving drum winding ropes on ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's capstan is a vertical drum rotated to wind in a cable, so it is something that rotates.

clue.text: Figure the second will create a row

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a figure
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A remark that a number in second place will cause an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' here, meaning a noise, not a line. 'will create' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clatter is a loud rattling din.

clue.text: Article written on more confusing hypothesis

indicators.note: in a down clue the article is written on top of what follows

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: confusing means mixing up, so the letters of more are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammatical article added to a more muddled theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' rearranges MORE into OREM; THE sits on top of it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a proposition to be proved, close to a supposition or proposal.

clue.text: Hot music that grows on one!

parts.note: h is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: Some hot music that you come to like the more you hear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grows on one' suggests something you warm to; read literally it is what grows on your head.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks sprout from the scalp, literally growing on a person.

clue.text: Liver possibly past its sell-by date, a pound

parts.note: food past its sell-by date has gone off
taken as written
l is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pound of liver bought cheaply because it has expired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' marks liver as just one example of organ meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal covers the edible internal organs of an animal, liver being one example.

clue.text: Take a chance joining a Greek character

parts.note: to take a chance is to bet

explanation.surface: Gambling on befriending a man from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person; it means a letter of the alphabet. 'joining' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A mere shade

definitions.meaning: a mere is a body of still water
a shade is a colour, here a crimson pigment

explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' reads as 'only'; it is the old word for a pond. LAKE is also a red pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is an inland pool of water, and lake is a deep red dye colour.

clue.text: Some seem used to being non-fliers

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people appear accustomed to never flying.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition, 'non-fliers', is a plural noun; 'to being' smooths the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian birds.

clue.text: Love to chatter about English work

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: the word for chatter goes about, enclosing the letter for English

parts.note: to prate is to chatter

explanation.surface: A fondness for gossiping about English literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside PRATE to make PERATE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, as a machine works.

clue.text: Getting out of such transport, people suffered capital loss

definitions.text: Getting out of such transport, people suffered capital loss

parts.words: Getting out of such transport, people suffered capital loss
parts.note: capital loss sounds financial, but it means losing one's head, as French revolutionaries did after arriving by cart at the guillotine

explanation.walkthrough: 'capital loss' sounds like finance; it means beheading. Carts carried the condemned to the guillotine in the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbril was the open cart that bore condemned prisoners to execution during the Terror.

clue.text: Coming by river, not all are daring

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
some is not all

explanation.surface: Arriving by water, only some of the travellers are bold.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire; 'by' and 'are' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventuresome means bold and willing to take risks, like adventurous.
